question: According to the text, what is the optimal growth temperature of many pathogenic mesophiles, and how does it relate to the human body temperature?
correct_answer: 37°C (98°F), which is the normal human body temperature
distractor1: 25°C (77°F), which is below the moderate range
distractor2: 40°C (104°F), which is the upper limit of the moderate range
support: Mesophiles grow best in moderate temperature, typically between 25°C and 40°C (77°F and 104°F). Mesophiles are often found living in or on the bodies of humans or other animals. The optimal growth temperature of many pathogenic mesophiles is 37°C (98°F), the normal human body temperature. Mesophilic organisms have important uses in food preparation, including cheese, yogurt, beer and wine.

question: According to the text, how would global winds blow without the Coriolis effect, and how does Coriolis alter their direction in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
correct_answer: Without Coriolis Effect the global winds would blow north to south or south to north; Coriolis makes them blow northeast to southwest or the reverse in the Northern Hemisphere and northwest to southeast or the reverse in the Southern Hemisphere.
distractor1: Without Coriolis Effect the global winds would blow east to west, and Coriolis makes them blow straight upward in both hemispheres.
distractor2: Without Coriolis Effect the global winds would blow northeast to southwest only in the Southern Hemisphere and northwest to southeast only in the Northern Hemisphere.
distractor3: Without Coriolis Effect the global winds would blow in circular storms only over oceans, with no directional difference by hemisphere.
support: Without Coriolis Effect the global winds would blow north to south or south to north. But Coriolis makes them blow northeast to southwest or the reverse in the Northern Hemisphere. The winds blow northwest to southeast or the reverse in the southern hemisphere.
